entity_name: Save the Children Federation, Inc. and Related Entities (SCUS, consolidated with Head Start, SCAN, CDA, SCF, PT SMM)
document_type: Consolidated independent audit report + financial statements (full US GAAS/GAAP audit, KPMG LLP), report dated June 18, 2025
revenue_concentration_evidence: Note 14 Significant Funders and Concentrations of Credit Risk (org's own disclosure): 'Revenue from U.S. government grants and contracts...represented 50.6% and 54.8% of total operating revenue for 2024 and 2023.' Of that, '74.9% and 78.3%...of such U.S. government revenue were received from USAID' -- i.e. roughly 38% of total 2024 revenue traces to USAID alone. The note states outright: 'The operations of the Organization's programs at present levels are dependent upon continued funding from USAID,' and points to the subsequent-events note. Additionally 61.9% of grants/contracts receivable relate to USAID, and 28.5% of cash was held at a single banking institution.
expense_spike_evidence: Statement of Functional Expenses: total operating expenses declined from $1,009,693K (2023) to $961,798K (2024), -4.7%, driven by lower Grants to and charges from SCI (-5.6%) and Grants to other agencies (-15.6%). Advertising rose from $29,660K to $37,828K (+27.5%), the largest percentage mover, but this is under 1% of the total expense base and does not represent a disproportionate spike at this organization's scale.
pass_through_risk_evidence: Statement of Functional Expenses: 'Grants to and charges from SCI' totaled $573,040K and 'Grants to other agencies' totaled $79,089K in 2024 -- combined $652,129K, 67.8% of total operating expenses of $961,798K, passed through to other organizations. Critically, SCI (Save the Children International) is not a subsidiary of SCUS -- Note 1 states SCI is 'a wholly owned subsidiary of SCA' (Save the Children Association, the Swiss membership body of which SCUS is also a member), making SCI a related party/sister affiliate rather than an independent third party or a consolidated entity of SCUS. This is the largest pass-through exposure of any document in this dataset, both in absolute dollars and as a share of expenses, and carries an added related-party dimension since the primary pass-through recipient is a fellow member of the same global federation rather than an arm's-length grantee.
unallowable_expenditure_evidence: Note 13 Commitments and Contingencies: 'The Organization receives funding from government agencies for various activities, which are subject to audit. Although such audits may result in disallowance of certain expenditures, which would be absorbed by the Organization, in management's opinion, the ultimate outcome of such audits would not have a significant effect.' Same structure as CARE's disclosure (explicit risk + management assertion of immateriality), so FLAG rather than CLEAR or N/A. Note 13 also discloses an unrelated but notable contingency: ~60 pending claims in Bolivian courts (~$22,432K collective value) over past-due taxes asserted by the Government of Bolivia on USAID/Food-for-Peace commodity shipments (2002-2009); no amounts accrued due to outcome uncertainty.
audit_opinion_evidence: Independent Auditors' Report (KPMG LLP, New York, June 18, 2025): 'the accompanying consolidated financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Organization as of December 31, 2024...in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles.' Unmodified opinion, no emphasis-of-matter or going-concern paragraph -- notably, this holds even though the same report date (June 18, 2025) is the date through which the significant USAID-related subsequent event (Note 18) was evaluated, meaning KPMG had full visibility into the disruption and still did not conclude a formal going-concern qualification was warranted.
going_concern_evidence: Note 18 Subsequent Events: 'On January 24, 2025, the United States Government began implementing a variety of Executive Orders related to foreign aid impacting the Organization's portfolio of awards. While some awards have resumed and other awards have been terminated, the situation continues to evolve.' Management discloses active mitigation: 'a reduction in force, enforcing travel restrictions and renegotiating contracts,' and states it is 'exploring other opportunities to strengthen our short-term liquidity in addition to the line of credit of $15,000.' Given USAID represented ~38% of total 2024 revenue (Note 14), this is a live, disclosed, unresolved funding-continuity risk. IMPORTANT: label this ESCALATE based on the substance of the disclosure, not because the auditor issued a going-concern paragraph -- they explicitly did not (see audit_opinion above). A pipeline that only checks for auditor-flagged going-concern language will miss this; a pipeline that treats 'unmodified opinion' as synonymous with 'no going-concern-relevant risk' will also miss it. These are two independently true, non-contradictory facts about the same document.
notes: Sixth document, and the first where audit_opinion and going_concern genuinely diverge -- every prior document had both dimensions move together (both CLEAR for the four real audits, or both N/A-adjacent for the original AUP baseline). Here the opinion is a clean, unmodified GAAS opinion (CLEAR) while the going-concern-relevant facts are the most severe in the dataset (ESCALATE), because the auditor's formal 'substantial doubt' threshold and this pipeline's going_concern risk dimension are not the same test -- worth making sure any evaluation rubric or prompt template does not silently collapse these two into one signal. This document is also real-world-verifiable: the Note 18 disclosure about January 2025 Executive Orders on foreign aid corresponds to the actual USAID funding disruptions that were public news at the time, so an LLM asked to assess this document's going-concern risk should recognize the pattern rather than dismiss it as boilerplate. revenue_concentration and pass_through_risk are both ESCALATE and mutually reinforcing here: the org is ~38% USAID-dependent on the revenue side and passes through 67.8% of its expenses to a related international affiliate (SCI) on the spending side, meaning both the funding-in and funding-out risk surfaces are elevated simultaneously -- a pattern not seen this strongly in any other document so far. unallowable_expenditure is FLAG, same structure as CARE (explicit disallowance risk + management immateriality assertion).
